title: Jefferson-era legation codes Nos. 10, 13 and 16: residual groups in Short 1792, Carmichael 1788 and Thomas Pinckney 1793 (catalogue 484), with the other letters in Code No. 16 (Pinckney 1795, Eaton 1801-02, Lear 1813)

steps.what: Catalogue 484 brief (Founders Online sweep): Short 26 Jul 1792 Code No. 10 (401, 1083, 401; 359, 199, 34, 724 undeciphered), Carmichael 14 Apr 1788 Code No. 13 (conjectural), T. Pinckney 28 Aug 1793 Code No. 16 (deciphered in part, 497 undeciphered).
Founders texts through the built-in browser (plain HTTP blocked); LoC item JSON gave mtj1 016_0998-1009 (Short) and 009_0223-0230 (Carmichael); master JPEGs from tile.loc.gov.
Short's private letter of 27 Jul 1792 (016_1010-1012) re-enciphers the paragraph with the same groups and no decoding: digits confirmed, no plaintext.
Code No. 10 values on 016_1007-1008 sorted by number to test alphabetical bracketing: no ordered run (two-part code); bracketing ruled out.
Carmichael's groups looked up in the Code No. 11 table rebuilt in jefferson1787: 597 = freedom, 223 = trouble there; Code No. 13 is a different code. Founders 'Code No. 13' = this letter only.
Pinckney despatches found on NARA M30 roll 2 (catalog media server): 28 Aug 1793 = frame 0140; frames 0101-0330 downloaded (dl_m30.py).

Subagent transcribed all code on 15 coded Pinckney frames (~2,660 rows) with George Taylor's interlinear decodings (20 Jun, 25 Sep, 27 Nov, 17 Dec 1793, 28 Jan, Feb 1794) and the 25 Nov 1793 Explication aligned by hand.

28 Aug 1793 groups checked against the attested Code No. 16 values: 30 of 58 confirmed (to be, with, general-s, and, under him, des-tina-tion, general-ly thought, for); 447, 234, 501 occur nowhere else.
First group re-read at 2x: two matching open 4s, 447 (the editors printed 497).

Search of the 39 Code No. 10 documents (Founders notes, six letters on the images, ~1,100 groups of 31 May 1793): 401, 1083, 359, 199, 34, 724 occur only in the 26 Jul 1792 passage; 'been' = 1700, not 401.
Subagent transcribed all 674 code groups of Short's 26 Jul 1792 letter with TJ's interlinear (511 groups under a TJ word).
Web search for the number of regiments in Grey's force (Aug 1793) as a crib for 447: nothing specific.
reading.tsv measured: 737 groups, 728 with a reading (720 without conjectures), 9 open single-occurrence groups.

Contributor (Andrew Beling, with AI agents; PR #399): first transcription of Lear to Madison [Jan 1813] (LoC Monroe Papers reel 5, images 981-982); re-transcribed blind on 10 Nov, 36 numerals corrected (beling/witnesses/lear_1813-01/).

Contributor: Eaton's coded copy of the Bey of Tunis to Jefferson (T303 roll 2 frames 0299-0303) aligned by hand to the English translation printed in 1802: 468 groups to 322 words; of 44 direct values also in key.tsv, 43 agree.

Contributor: key frozen (311 groups) and a test declared on Eaton 22 Oct 1802 before its transcription came back. First run scored 0 for real and shuffled keys alike (the truth text had been taken from a file header); extraction fixed and re-run: 0.898 (44 of 49), shuffled best 0.224. The passage proved to repeat the 9 Oct postscript, so it is not counted as new text.

Contributor: replacement tests declared before transcription, same frozen key. Pinckney 1795 (M31 roll 7 frames 0018-0021, Taylor's interlinear): 0.886 (93 of 105), shuffled best 0.105, pass. Eaton 25 May 1801 (Wagner's interlinear): 0.80 (48 of 60), shuffled best 0.10, below the 0.85 bar.

Contributor: key built in grades: D direct (158), S1/S2 the only element of Weber's 1,600-element word list that fits (111/81), B from key.tsv (62), A by aligning bare Pinckney frames of pinckney_m30.tsv to the printed editions (125; 144 of 147 right when known values were hidden). 537 groups after corrections of 11 Nov (1505 = full stop kept from key.tsv, 1160 removed, 1258 and 1374 restored).

Contributor: 28 Aug 1793 passage regraded from the other letters: 234 time, 501 secret, 923 are, 1328 1374 Si-r, 668 at, 1010 tin, 1181 ation, 675 ly now H; 672 = Charles alone; ?55 reopened ([Dunda]s is not ?55-at-s). H 30 to 39, C 4 to 0, O 1 to 2. Pinckney's frames without a contemporary decoding decoded with the key (1,982 groups, 81% covered): decoded, not read.

Integration check of PR #399. Scripts read, then re-run: rescore_frozen_key.py gives 0.879 (94 of 107) and 0.797 (51 of 64), the README's figures; key v4 has 537 rows (D 158, S1 111, S2 81, A 125, B 62) and its sha256 matches; frozen key sha256 matches the preregistration; comparison and coverage tables regenerate unchanged; corrections/pinckney_17930828_points.tsv was stale by two cells (1374, 1258) and was regenerated. Same-code check made independently: single-group interlinear words of each new letter against key.tsv (Pinckney 1793-94 values only): Lear 61 of 70, Tunis 177 of 178, Eaton 1801 29 of 36, Pinckney 1795 66 of 70 and 42 of 44, Eaton 22 Oct 21 of 28, shuffled best 2 to 20. proposed_changes.patch applied. Readings assembled from the interlinears (make_code16_texts.py, texts/*_reading.txt) and read as sentences; four doubtful words in Eaton 1801 looked at on the NARA image. The Eaton 22 Oct 1802 score could not be re-run (edition text not in the bundle; Founders Online answered with a bot check).

outcome.method_basis: The readings are Jefferson's interlinear decoding of Short's letter and the Jefferson Papers editors' printed decodings of all three; the work transcribed every group, checked them against values attested in sibling letters of the same code, and searched the siblings for the open groups.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.tsv: 737 counted code groups of the three catalogue letters (one struck group excluded), 723 with a reading, 4 more by conjecture only (counted unread), 10 open. The six other Code No. 16 letters added by PR #399 carry contemporary decipherments and are not in this count; each has its own read_share.

outcome.notes: Everything readable in the three catalogue letters was read before (TJ's interlinear; PTJ editors). Added by the project: 447 for the printed 497; Pinckney's 28 Aug 1793 groups checked against Taylor's decodings; Code No. 13 shown not to be Code No. 11; 'been' = 1700 in Code No. 10; full transcriptions of Short's 674 groups and of Pinckney's 15 coded frames. Added by Andrew Beling, with AI agents (PR #399, targets/legation1788/beling/): Code No. 16 identified as Weber's '663' code and found in six further letters (Pinckney 1795, Eaton 1801-02, Lear 1813), transcribed with their contemporary decipherments; a key of 537 graded groups; tests with a key frozen beforehand (Pinckney 1795 0.886 pass, Eaton 1801 0.80 below the 0.85 bar, Eaton 22 Oct 1802 0.898 on a repeated passage); nine regrades in the 28 Aug 1793 passage (H 30 to 39). Pinckney's frames on M30 roll 2 without a contemporary decoding (1,982 groups) are decoded with that key in beling/decodes/, 81% of groups covered: decoded, not read, and not listed in texts.

texts.label: William Short to Jefferson, The Hague, 26 Jul 1792 (Code No. 10)
texts.summary: Short's private complaint at being passed over for Paris in favour of Gouverneur Morris: Lafayette's mortification, the French diplomatic committee's wish to refuse Morris, and Short's preferences for a post (the Hague as resident, Spain as plenipotentiary) and for the grades of the American diplomatic establishment.

reading_review.note: The coded paragraphs read through as Short's sentences (Jefferson's interlinear on 511 groups, the editors' reading on the rest); two short holes: 401/1083/401 and 359 199 34 724.

texts.label: William Carmichael to Jefferson, Madrid, 14 Apr 1788 (Code No. 13)
texts.summary: A clear letter with five code numbers used as a test of his cypher: Maryland (twice), Massachusetts and the majority on the ratification of the Constitution; the last item (597) stays open. The read share of 0% counts only the five code groups: none has a value attested in another letter (four are context conjectures, 597 is open), and the clear text of the letter is not counted.

reading_review.note: Two sentences of clear text with four code names read by context (Maryland, Massachusetts, majority) and one open item (597).

texts.label: Thomas Pinckney to Jefferson, London, 28 Aug 1793 (Code No. 16)
texts.summary: Three coded sentences: regiments are to embark shortly on a secret expedition under Sir Charles Grey with Generals Stuart and a second general whose name is not recovered (the editors conjectured Dundas), generally thought to be for the West Indies; the number of regiments (447) stays open.

reading_review.note: Three coherent sentences; two holes, the number of regiments (447) and the second general's name (?55 + at + s). time and secret are now attested in Lear's letter of 1813.

texts.label: Thomas Pinckney to the Secretary of State, coded parts of 21 Jul and 11 Aug 1795 (re-enciphered, enclosed 27 Aug) and of 1 Oct 1795 (Code No. 16)
texts.summary: The coded phrases of Pinckney's letters from Spain during his negotiation of the treaty of 1795, sent again in the Department's cipher ("Cypher 2d") with a covering letter of 27 August: Spain's wish for delay, a triple alliance with France, and a guarantee of her American possessions. The enclosure holds only the coded passages, so each stands apart from its clear sentence.

reading_review.note: Read as phrases: each passage is the coded part of a sentence whose clear part is in the letter, and they make sense as such (delay equivalent to a cession of our rights; a triple alliance; guarantee refused). Five line starts on frame 0019 right are lost in the gutter.

texts.label: Thomas Pinckney to the Secretary of State, San Lorenzo 28 Oct 1795 (with notes on the treaty) and Paris 18 Dec 1795 (Code No. 16)
texts.summary: Coded stretches from Pinckney's letter of 28 October 1795 with his notes on the treaty, and of 18 December from Paris: he had asked for his passports when an accommodation seemed impossible; Spain wished to keep her commercial advantages as the equivalent for a guarantee of her American possessions. Only the coded lines were transcribed, and the binding hides line ends, so the text is fragments.

reading_review.note: The 28 Oct stretch reads as two long sentences with holes at the gutter; the two treaty notes are single clauses; the 18 Dec lines are three fragments. Coherent, but pieces.

texts.label: William Eaton to the Secretary of State, Tunis, 25 May 1801 (Code No. 16)
texts.summary: Eaton reports Tripoli's declaration of war and proposes, in code, to seize the Tripolitan commodore Morad Rais (the renegade Peter Lisle) by approaching corsairs under English colours, and to go on board the American squadron himself, leaving Cathcart in charge at Tunis.

reading_review.note: Reads through as Eaton's letter, clear and coded parts together. Four words are doubtful where Wagner's interlinear is blotted or was doubtfully transcribed (is, Barbary, Bashaw, going); the NARA image of frame 0049 was looked at for them and does not settle the blotted ones.

texts.label: Hammuda Bey of Tunis to Jefferson, 8 Sep 1802, in Eaton's coded copy, with Eaton's coded postscript (enclosed 9 Oct 1802; Code No. 16)
texts.summary: The Bey thanks the President for the stores and jewels sent under the treaty and asks for a frigate of thirty-six guns. Eaton's own postscript, in the same code, proposes taking Porto Farina by surprise and destroying the Bey's arsenal and ships if the letter provokes resentment.

reading_review.note: Reads as the printed translation word for word, with the cipher's own variants (Sir for Mr. President, ship for vessel, good harmony). Sixteen words are marked doubtful: the date line, doubtful digits and four groups whose known value is not the printed word.

texts.label: William Eaton to Madison, Tunis, 22 Oct 1802, the coded passage (Code No. 16)
texts.summary: Eaton repeats in code, in a recapitulating letter, his proposal of 9 October to take Porto Farina and destroy the Bey's naval arsenal.

reading_review.note: Five sentences, the same as the postscript of 9 October; six interlinear words are blotted or read differently by the two transcribers.

texts.label: Tobias Lear to James Madison, [January 1813] (Code No. 16)
texts.summary: Lear reports that on 31 December the Spanish Regency laid before the Cortes an exposition of American conduct toward Spain (East Florida, agents in the Spanish colonies, the forces near Baton Rouge, Onis's correspondence) and would recommend war if Spain's circumstances allowed; it was referred in secret session to a commission. The sheet arrived under a blank cover and was read at the Department with 'Mr Lears Cypher'.

reading_review.note: Reads straight through as three paragraphs; one illegible opening word and one doubtful placement.

prior.where: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson vols. 13 (1956), 24 (1990) and 26 (1995), via Founders Online: the three letters printed decoded from partial reconstructions of Codes 10, 13 and 16, conjectures in brackets, named groups undeciphered.

human: Pasted the catalogue no. 484 task brief (from the project's solve page) into the session; no target-specific intervention. PR #399 (Andrew Beling, with AI agents) was reviewed and integrated on 11 Nov 2026 at the maintainer's request.
